newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - CZECH CROWN JITTERY, SEEN MOVING LOWER.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - CZECH CROWN JITTERY, SEEN MOVING LOWER.

text.p: The Czech crown's jittery performance on Wednesday could signify the beginning of a long and slow decline in the currency's fortunes although a sharp depreciation is unlikely, dealers said.

Just after trading open, the crown dropped by nearly 50 basis points against the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket to +3.2 percent, after a local newspaper report said that several German banks expected the crown to weaken.

A few minutes later, the currency recovered slightly after the Statistical Bureau relased results of a survey of local importers and exporters showing that most expected a trade deficit in the first quarter of 45 billion crowns compared with just 27.1 billion in the same period in 1996.
Dealers acknowledged there was an irony in seeing such a poor trade forecast as reassuring, but the crown's volatility reflected general nervousness of a market grasping for signals.
"The market here is just nervous. The last 14 days have seen growing rumours about the Czech crown," said Jakub Perina of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
"There is no strong background with economic fundamentals to make the crown stronger," he added.

From Christmas to early February, the crown gained roughly three percentage points over parity with the basket, spurred by nearly 40 billion crowns worth of crown denominated Eurobonds, issued because of relatively high Czech interest rates.
At the crown's peak earlier this month it rose to +5.5 percent over parity before talk about central bank intervention jolted the markets, forcing the currency below +4.0 percent.

"I think that there has been some feeling in the last 2-3 weeks, probably it's a little psychlogical..but the crown could go lower. We can't really expect (plus) four to five percent again (over parity)," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka.
"By the end of the first half of the year we could go further with some depreciation," Becvar added.

The recent decline of the crown has been actively encouraged by the Czech National Bank which has so far only tried to talk it lower by saying the wave of Eurobonds was irrational and that interest rate cuts were a possibility.
The central bank fixed the crown at 28.452 to the dollar after Tuesday's fixing at 28.345, and at 17.032 to the mark from 16.907, still following the market.
The above rates imply a deviation from the midpoint of the central bank's mark/dollar basket of +3.47 percent, after a deviation of +4.05 on Tuesday.
The one year Prague InterBank Offered Rate (PRIBOR) stood at 11.23 percent on Wednesday.
